profile.name: Shahir Ahmed
profile.title: Software Engineer
profile.summary: Software engineer and M.S. Computer Science student at New York University. Previously a software engineer at Sarva and a software engineer intern on FarmData2. Ranked 31st of 800+ contributors to Mermaid.js.

highlights: Cut inventory update time by 60% by building a multilingual AI voice assistant in Next.js and TypeScript that lets store owners add or update multiple products by voice over WebRTC
Reduced zero-result searches by 17% by adding semantic search with OpenAI embeddings and Firestore vector queries to Algolia keyword search so shoppers can find products using natural language
Built a Stripe Connect payout system for vendors and drivers with Google Cloud Functions that retry failed transfers and use idempotency keys to prevent duplicate payments
Prevented overselling during concurrent checkouts by checking and reserving stock in atomic Firestore transactions
Created GitHub Actions CI/CD pipelines that run 2,604 Vitest tests and check preview deployments before release
Built the product that put Sarva in the gener8tor and Meta gBETA accelerator and the Ship Tank and launchU finals
experience.summary: Startup that helps neighborhood grocery shops manage inventory by voice, with online ordering, pickup, and delivery.

highlights: Developed crop seeding and tillage tracking in Vue.js through 25 merged pull requests to a National Science Foundation (NSF) funded open source platform that supports sustainability research and helps farmers manage field operations
Protected crop records with JavaScript rollback handlers that undo earlier writes when farmOS REST API calls fail
Wrote 70+ Cypress unit, integration, and end-to-end tests for data validation, record creation, and API failure recovery
experience.summary: Paid internship on open source farm record-keeping software funded by the National Science Foundation.

highlights: Added diagram features and fixed rendering bugs in TypeScript and D3.js for a library with 15M+ weekly downloads: data labels inside bar charts, Knuth-Plass word wrapping that keeps journey diagram legends from overlapping the diagram, and journey diagram title styling
Authored 3 merged pull requests with 22 Cypress regression tests by collaborating with maintainers and contributors
Ranked 31st of 800+ contributors on the repository's contributor graph as of October 2026
experience.summary: Open source tool that turns text into flowcharts and diagrams, used by GitHub and Microsoft.

highlights: Built an ANTLR4 parser and abstract syntax tree (AST) translator to convert CBASIC into Python and Java
Co-designed a migration plan for 50,000+ lines of legacy code with 11 Dickinson students and 84 Lumber engineers
Taught 25+ students to write and debug Python and Java programs through labs, code reviews, and office hours
Mediated roommate conflicts, handled on-call emergencies, and connected 40 residents with campus resources

projects.name: GrabPic
projects.description: Event photo search. Upload a selfie to find your photos in albums of 500+ photos, matched in under 200 milliseconds. Three services (Next.js, Spring Boot, Python DeepFace/TensorFlow worker) connected through Amazon SQS, with pgvector HNSW search, S3 presigned uploads, per-IP Redis rate limiting in an atomic Lua script, and Cloudflare Turnstile. The backend is self-hosted on Shahir's home server, cutting hosting from about $85 to about $1 a month.

projects.name: PaperPulse
projects.description: Research assistant that picks the 25 most relevant new papers from arXiv, PubMed, Semantic Scholar, and OpenAlex for each user every night, ranked with neural reranking, and answers questions about them with retrieval augmented generation over pgvector and a Neo4j knowledge graph, streaming responses over Server-Sent Events. FastAPI and Next.js, with the backend self-hosted in Docker.

projects.name: Home Server
projects.description: Self-hosted cloud on an Acer Nitro 5 laptop running Ubuntu Server. Runs the GrabPic, PaperPulse, and Queue Up backends in Docker behind Cloudflare Tunnel for about $1 a month instead of about $100 on AWS, with no inbound ports open. Coolify deploys from GitHub and configures Traefik routes, private apps are reachable only over Tailscale, Uptime Kuma monitors every app, and a live Next.js page streams host and container status with Server-Sent Events.

projects.name: Queue Up
projects.description: Social app that matches people by Spotify listening history, with real-time WebSocket chat. Spring Boot, React, PostgreSQL, Docker, self-hosted on Shahir's home server.

projects.name: CoSign
projects.description: Task accountability app where users can't complete their own tasks. A verifier approves submitted proof through a task state machine, and missed deadlines automatically email the AES-encrypted hidden penalty to the verifier. Spring Boot, React, TypeScript, WebSockets, Docker.

projects.name: PandOS
projects.description: Operating system kernel in C for the uMPS3 emulator that runs up to 20 processes on 5 ms round-robin time slices, with semaphores, TLB-based virtual memory, system calls, and interrupt handling.

projects.name: BitTorrent Client JS
projects.description: BitTorrent client in Node.js for .torrent files and magnet links, with TCP peer connections, SHA-1 piece verification, and extension protocol metadata exchange.

projects.name: Albatross
projects.description: Built at HackHarvard 2024 after two teammates had felt unsafe walking through parts of Boston. Navigation app that routes walkers around high crime areas, built by a team of 4 in 36 hours, using 50K+ crime records grouped into risk zones with MLflow and Databricks. Vue.js, Cloudflare Workers, Google Maps API.

projects.name: SweetFriend
projects.description: Built at PennApps 2024 with a teammate who lives with type 1 diabetes. Dexcom glucose data on a Chart.js timeline (Shahir's React frontend), GPT-4o meal photo carb estimates via Tune Studio, a Cerebras chatbot, Twilio alerts, and a Flask and MongoDB backend.

projects.name: Prospectus
projects.description: Shahir's first hackathon (HoyaHacks 2024). The team designed an AI college admissions assistant with React, Django, and Azure OpenAI, but did not finish a working product in time.

honors: Pi Mu Epsilon (National Mathematics Honor Society)
